This report is requesting approval of the twenty twenty two internal audit plan.
In accordance with the approved internal audit charter, the city internal auditor's office has developed a twenty twenty two internal audit plan.
A comprehensive internal audit risk assessment was conducted in the development of the plan.
Based on the approach used in applying professional judgment and audit plan was developed focusing on high risk auditable areas.
The audits have been classified into three types internal controls value for money and information technology.
For the year twenty twenty two four audits have been planned.
If resources and time permit, additional audits will be undertaken in twenty twenty two subject to approval of the standing policy committee on finance.
The audit plan will be a flexible plan to respond to emerging risk as year progresses.
The plan twenty twenty two audits in order of priority includes continuous assurance project management processes including vendor performance management.
Fusion way one implementation and fleet services.
In addition, Intel audit will also be undertaking whistleblower investigation status updates and full of activities on past audit recommendations and ongoing advisory services.
For twenty twenty three six audits have planned subject to change.
These include fire rescue operations, procure to pay process, cooperate asset management, employ payroll process, cyber security program assessment and waste services.
To execute the plan, a combination of in-house and external resources will be utilized.
The city internal auditors office will be responsible for the effectiveness and timeliness of all audits including co-sourced audits.
I would like to highlight the first three audits shown in the appendix one.
The first audit is continuous assurance.
This audit will analyze large volumes of data using technology on an ongoing basis to provide assurance whether processes and controls are operating.
As intended.
It will provide assurance on the whole population and closer to the occurrence of transactions.
Thus any errors, non-compliances and fraud risks will be detected on a timely basis and at times before the money leaves the city.
Internal audit will implement continuous assurance in areas such as procurement, vendor payments, payroll, expense reimbursements, corporate credit cards etc.
The second audit is project management processes.
The city spends millions of dollars every year on capital projects and it is important that the city has strong project management processes in place,
including vendor performance management.
This audit will assess the project management practices and would recommend ways to strengthen it.
The third audit is Fusion Way One Implementation.
Fusion is a single largest transformational project that the city is currently implementing.
This audit will take a 50,000 foot view to assess the success of the way one implementation which comprised of supply chain, finance and payroll modules.
The audit will evaluate areas such as automation of processes and controls, staff training, manual workarounds, governance, tracking and resolution of issues, access to systems,
monitoring and reporting.
